findings.evidence: "The IT asset group updates the reimbursement log at the start of the fiscal year... the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month."
findings.fix: Choose one publication schedule. Either the catalog is published annually at fiscal year start, or it is updated monthly on the first business day, and revise both statements to match.
findings.violation: The document contradicts itself about when the equipment catalog is maintained. Line 7 says it is tracked on the first business day of each month, but line 61 states the finance liaison publishes it at the start of the fiscal year.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Replace "You must" with "Employees must" and "we may" with "the benefits team may" to maintain consistent voice throughout.
findings.violation: The document switches from third-person reference to "you" and "we", inconsistent with earlier sections that refer to "employees" and "the policy".

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests... employees must retain receipts for one year after the purchase date."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the photo is the only documentation retained long-term, or whether full receipts must also be kept, and whether one-year retention is mandatory for all requests.
findings.violation: It is unclear whether employees need to retain full receipts or only photos, and whether this one-year retention is a requirement or optional.

findings.evidence: "the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Clarify the relationship between "one device per category" and "one claim per benefit year" - either consolidate into one clear rule or explain how both limits apply together.
findings.violation: This appears to contradict line 11 which states "The stipend covers one claim per employee per benefit year". It is unclear whether the limits are per category or per benefit year.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form... Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Add a definition of "stipend item" in the Terminology Notes section, or rename the term to something clearer like "equipment request" or "reimbursement request".
findings.violation: The term "stipend item" is used multiple times but is never defined. It is unclear whether this refers to the equipment, the dollar amount, the request itself, or something else.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Either expand Request Steps to list all required steps in order, or remove this section and cross-reference the other sections that describe the actual workflow.
findings.violation: This section lists only two steps, but earlier sections describe additional steps including manager review, confirmation summary review, and equipment category verification. The Request Steps section appears incomplete.

findings.evidence: "You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Replace "You track" with "Employees track" to maintain consistent third-person voice.
findings.violation: The document switches to second-person "you" here, inconsistent with the third-person voice used in most other sections.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Clarify whether the $200 threshold is a decision point that creates different approval workflows, or move this detail to the Approval Timeline section with clear context about when this review occurs.
findings.violation: A $200 review threshold is introduced here for the first time, but it contradicts the $500 maximum benefit previously stated and there is no explanation of why requests under $200 are not reviewed.

findings.evidence: "the IT asset group tracks the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month. A copy of each update goes to the shared benefits folder the same day."
findings.fix: Remove the redundant statement or clarify that the tracking update and the copy distribution to the benefits folder are a single coordinated action, not two separate actions.
findings.violation: The statement that a copy goes to the shared benefits folder "the same day" is redundant given that the tracking happens on the first business day. This creates ambiguity about whether these are the same action or two separate actions.
